subject.title: Self-host: local console sign-in without Cloudflare Access (follow-up to #95 / #104)

question: Should local token-backed browser sessions become a supported opt-in capability of the Docker self-host profile?
rationale: This adds a persistent browser-authentication mode and configuration surface beyond the existing bearer-token administration workflow, so implementation quality alone cannot establish the supported product contract.

options.title: Sponsor the opt-in local-auth path
options.body: Review https://github.com/openclaw/clawrouter/pull/106 as the narrow implementation, retaining Cloudflare Access as the managed-deployment path.

options.title: Keep self-host API-only
options.body: Retain the current bearer-token administration workflow and close the feature direction without adding browser sessions.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the opt-in local-auth path
recommendation.body: Review https://github.com/openclaw/clawrouter/pull/106 as the narrow implementation, retaining Cloudflare Access as the managed-deployment path.

likelyOwner.reason: The current self-host profile and its stated console-session limitation were introduced in the merged self-host work.
